items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: So Cootie said to him, "Well, Charlie, you play the first chair until my man gets here."

ctx.x: He says, "I've got a man, I've got a man. He's coming here from Texas." I said, "From Texas?" Well, I had never known no great first saxophone men from Texas! They have a whole lot of good saxophone players from Texas, but they weren't what they would call a lead man, you know? They were all what you'd call get-off men. They could solo and everything else. But not no lead. So I said, "Okay, all right. Third part's good for me."

So Cootie started rehearsing the band. He sent out a notice for different musicians and one-thing-or-another. And he started rehearsing. Well, the lead saxophone player wasn't there at the first rehearsal. So Cootie said to him, "Well, Charlie, you play the first chair until my man gets here." You know, to see(?) (?). And in the meantime, he was trying out other men that was standing around with their horns. Everybody was trying out. And Cootie was very generous. He had plenty of whiskey there. And it was just…

So we would rehearse a number, and then we'd stop and take a break, have a little taste and so forth. Well, they would take up the afternoon, you know, take up the time, and come back the next day. Well, we kept on rehearsing. So I say to Cootie, I said, "Well, Cootie, when is your lead saxophone player coming?" He said, "Well, he'll be here

items.title: 56712_Cootie Williams oral history interview
items.q: Well, when you had Charlie Holmes, cause it's in a sense like having Johnny in a way.

ctx.x: And that's the reason why I had it.
Yeah. That's terrific. Well, when you had Charlie Holmes, cause it's in a sense like having Johnny in a way.
